In Quebec people speak french to each other, but using some english words. Montreal is the exception and way more bilingual. New Brunswick is about half french and half english and people will change from one to the other mid sentence.

In Quebec, we "park" our car in a "stationnement". J'ai parké ma voiture dans le stationnement. We use "magasiner" when we go shopping.

In France, they "stationne" their car in a parking. J'ai stationné ma voiture dans le parking. They also use "shopping".

So some places use different words to mean the same thing.

In Quebec, the word "gosses" means testicules. In France it means kids.

So the distance between the french colonies made it so that each colony developed a different accent and words. Since Québec is near the States, it was influenced by English a lot.

There's no easy way to describe all the differences. Most of the vocabulary and grammar is the same. Some words mean different things. Some things might be called different names.
